open-question.question: Today a DONE with nothing staged is a no-op the whole-index guard absorbs; once the change set travels as a file, an absent or empty file after DONE is a distinct condition, an agent that completed the task but wrote no path list, which a guard on the file's paths cannot tell from a task that changed nothing. When an agent returns DONE and its path file is absent or empty, does the orchestrator take the task as having produced no committable change, or stop the run on a fixed stop line of its own?
open-question.recommendation: With the agent listing the two task files every DONE's file holds at least the two paths the move just changed, so an absent or empty file is a broken return contract and never a change-free task; stopping keeps the move and the edits out of a later task's commit, and the fixed-line convention gives the check that ended the run its own identifier-free line rather than the no-status line, which misdescribes a DONE.
open-question.alternative: An absent and an empty path file are both a stop condition: the orchestrator commits nothing, ends the run, and prints a new fixed identifier-free stop line of its own (one new row in the fixed-lines table and its test), with the task name and which of absent or empty it found on the lines below. The tree is left as the agent left it, resumable, with the move and the edits uncommitted. A broken return contract is never absorbed silently: the operator or a harness sees a distinct, matchable line naming exactly this condition, and nothing is committed under a change set the orchestrator cannot vouch for. A task that legitimately changed nothing beyond the task list stops a headless run if an empty file is how it reports that, which depends on whether the agent's file lists the two task files (then an empty file is never legitimate) or the orchestrator adds them (then it can be), a sibling's axis; it also adds a fixed line, a table row, and a test.

An absent and an empty path file after DONE are both taken as a task that produced no committable change: the orchestrator commits nothing for that task, creates no empty commit, goes on to the next task, and counts the task toward the run's committed-nothing no-op line exactly as today's whole-index guard does for a DONE with nothing staged. No new console line is added. A long headless run is never interrupted by a return-file slip, and the orchestrator keeps today's semantics for a DONE that brought nothing to commit, so neither the fixed-lines table nor any harness matching it changes. A task the agent did complete, moving its section in TASKS_TODO.md and TASKS_DONE.md and editing project files, is left uncommitted with nothing reported; because every later commit is pathspec-bound, the stranded project edits never ride into a commit and stay dirty, while the moved task files ride into the next task's Task-completion: commit (wherever the task files are named, a sibling's axis) and misattribute the move, or stay dirty after the last task.

An absent and an empty path file are both taken as a task with no project change, but the orchestrator still commits the two task files it can name from the milestone directory it holds, TASKS_TODO.md and TASKS_DONE.md, under Task-completion: <Task Title>, and goes on to the next task. No stop and no new console line; any project edits the agent made but did not list stay uncommitted in the tree. The task's completion is always recorded in its own commit, so the move never leaks into the next task's commit, and the run continues uninterrupted for a task that genuinely touched only the task list. A missing list silently splits a task's change set: its section lands as done in history while its project edits stay dirty and unattributed, exactly the change silently left out of a commit the path file exists to prevent; a later task's agent may then take them up under the resumption rule as earlier or another run's work.

An absent and an empty path file are both a stop, reported through the existing no-status condition: a DONE without a usable path file is treated as a return with no usable status, so the run stops on the existing line `Task run stopped — a task agent returned no status.` with the task name and what was missing below it, commits nothing, and leaves the tree resumable. No new fixed line is added; the condition's test is widened from the message alone to the message plus its file. The failure is caught and stops the run without growing the fixed-lines contract, so a harness already matching the no-status stop handles the new case with no change. The line misdescribes the case, since the agent did return DONE and the task's move is already in the tree, and one line now covers two checks, against the convention that each stop condition opens with a line of its own; a harness or operator reading it as a model failure looks in the wrong place.

The two cases are told apart: the agent always writes the path file, empty when it changed nothing beyond the task list, so an absent file is a breach of its return contract and stops the run on a new fixed stop line of its own (task name below, nothing committed, tree resumable), while an empty file is a task with no project change and the orchestrator commits only the two task files it names from the milestone directory, then continues. A contract breach and a genuinely change-free task get different, correct handling: the breach is never absorbed, and a verification-only or documentation-free task neither stops a headless run nor leaves its move uncommitted. It is coherent only if the orchestrator rather than the agent supplies the task files (if the agent lists them, an empty file is as much a breach as an absent one), a sibling's axis; and an agent that wrote the file but forgot to record its edits still passes as change-free, its edits left dirty, while the agent contract gains the always-write rule and the fixed-lines table one row.

The two cases are told apart as in the split above: the agent always writes the path file, an empty file commits only the two task files the orchestrator names from the milestone directory and the run continues, and an absent file stops the run, but through the existing no-status condition and its line `Task run stopped — a task agent returned no status.` rather than a new one, the missing file below it, nothing committed, tree resumable. It keeps the split's correct handling of a change-free task while adding no fixed line, since a DONE whose promised file never appeared is reported as the incomplete return it is. It shares the split's dependence on the orchestrator supplying the task files (a sibling's axis) and its blindness to an empty file that omits real edits, and the reused line still says no status where the agent said DONE, one line standing for two checks.

open-question.question: The orchestrator's no-op line `Task run committed nothing — no task staged a change.` names staging, which the agent no longer does, and a fixed line is a contract harnesses match across versions, changing only together with its row in the fixed-lines table. Does the line keep its wording unchanged, or is it reworded to stop naming the retired mechanism?
open-question.recommendation: With the task files always in the agent's file and a missing or empty file a stop, every DONE the orchestrator commits from carries the two paths the move just changed, so a run that commits nothing cannot occur and the line would promise harnesses an outcome that never happens; retiring it with its table row ends the stale staging wording without spending a whole-line contract change on a rewording.
open-question.alternative: The committed-nothing condition, its fixed line, and its row in the fixed-lines table are removed. A run whose tasks all returned `DONE` always ends on `All tasks completed.`, and step 2c's per-task guard either stays as a silent skip or goes with the line. `tests/test_fixed_console_lines.py` needs no change of its own, because it checks only the rows the table lists. It removes a line describing a condition the new commit call cannot reach. Every `DONE` follows a successful `move`, which changes `TASKS_TODO.md` and `TASKS_DONE.md`, and those files reach the commit one way or another, so a whole run with nothing committed cannot happen. The plugin then stops promising harnesses an outcome that never occurs, and the stale wording question goes away with it. A harness matching the line loses it with no replacement, and an outcome that was listed simply disappears from the contract. Whether the condition is truly unreachable depends on the sibling questions on whether the task files reach the commit through the path file or from the orchestrator's own directory, and on what a missing or empty path file after `DONE` means. If the line is retired and a reachable case is left, the run would print the success line over a run that committed nothing.

The no-op line stays byte-for-byte `Task run committed nothing — no task staged a change.`, in `core/skills/complete-all-tasks/SKILL.md` and in its row of `docs/skill-reference.md`'s `## Fixed console lines` table alike. Only the prose around it changes: the sentence introducing the line, and the step-2c guard it summarizes, are rewritten for the commit-from-file call, while the printed line itself still says "staged". No harness matching the line across versions breaks, and nothing in the fixed-lines table, `tests/test_fixed_console_lines.py`, or any host tree needs touching for it. That keeps the contract the table exists to provide, under which a line changes only when it has to. The line names a mechanism the milestone retires. Once the agent stops staging, "no task staged a change" describes nothing that happens in the run. A reader or harness author would take it at face value, and it would disagree with the reworded `docs/workflow.md`, `docs/skill-reference.md`, and the committing invariant, which will no longer say anything is staged by the agent.

The line keeps its opening clause `Task run committed nothing —` and only the reason after the dash is reworded to name no git or hand-off mechanism, for example `Task run committed nothing — no task changed a file.` The reworded line replaces the old one in `complete-all-tasks` and in its fixed-lines table row in the same change, and `tests/test_fixed_console_lines.py` then checks the new text in every host tree. The line stops naming the retired mechanism and names none to replace it, so it survives the draft's later milestones changing how a change set travels again. Keeping the prefix lets a harness that matches on the clause before the dash keep working. This matches the shape of sibling no-op lines such as `complete-task`'s `No task completed — no file changed.` Any harness matching the whole line, which is the form the table and the test define, breaks on upgrade and has to update its match. A one-time contract change is spent on wording alone, for a condition that is rarely if ever reached, because a successful move always changes the two task files.

The line is reworded to name the mechanism that replaces staging: the paths each agent writes to its file in the run's scratch directory. An example is `Task run committed nothing — no task recorded a changed path.` It is changed together with its fixed-lines table row and checked by `tests/test_fixed_console_lines.py` as in any rewording. It says exactly what the orchestrator's guard checks under the new design, so the line keeps describing the run's real mechanism the way the old one did when it was written. A reader who sees it knows to look at the agents' path files, not at the index. It breaks whole-line harness matches just as any rewording does, and it ties the line to a mechanism again, so a later change to how the change set travels would force another rewording. Its accuracy also depends on the sibling questions on whether the path file lists the task files and on how a missing or empty path file is handled. If a missing file is treated as no committable change, "recorded" no longer holds for that case.
